newsitem.title: USA: ORGANOGENESIS BEGINS MAKING SKIN EQUIVALENT.
newsitem.headline: ORGANOGENESIS BEGINS MAKING SKIN EQUIVALENT.

text.p: Organogenesis Inc said on Monday that it had begun commercial manufacture of Apligraf, a human skin equivalent, for treatment of venous ulcers in Canada.

Apligraf, approved for venous ulcers in April by the Health Protection Branch of Canada, is the first living, manufactured human organ approved for marketing by a major regulatory agency, Organogenesis said in a statement.

"Apligraf is a major breakthrough in chronic wound management and, as such, should revolutionize the treatment of these expensive and debilitating skin ulcers," said Dr R. Gary Sibbald, associate professor of medicine at the University of Toronto.
Apligraf was launched by the Novartis Pharmaceuticals Canada Inc affiliate of Novartis AG, which has global marketing rights to the product.
Organogenesis, which develops living organ equivalents, is responsible for supplying Novartis Pharmaceuticals' global requirements for Apligraf.
